nodes.name: Run collection
nodes.notes: Start here: click 'Execute workflow' to run the whole collection stage once. In Week 3 the orchestrator will call this stage instead.

parameters.jsCode:
// ==== Fill in once ==========================================================
const DRIVE_FILE_IDS = {          // Google Drive file IDs of the 5 CSVs
  orders: 'PASTE_ID',
  order_items: 'PASTE_ID',
  customers: 'PASTE_ID',
  sellers: 'PASTE_ID',
  geolocation: 'PASTE_ID',
};
const SPREADSHEET_ID = 'PASTE_ID';  // the "Olist product list" Google Sheet
const MOCK_API_URL = 'http://localhost:5678/webhook/olist-mock-api';  // Production URL of the mock API
const ONLY = [];  // to test a few sources, e.g. ['sellers', 'products']; empty = all 9
// ============================================================================

const runId = 'collect_' + new Date().toISOString().replace(/[-:T]/g, '').slice(0, 14);

// Smallest first, geolocation last: problems show up early and cheaply
const sources = [
  { source: 'category_translation', type: 'sheet', table: 'category_translation_sheet', tab: 'category_translation' },
  { source: 'sellers', type: 'csv', table: 'sellers_csv', file: 'sellers.csv' },
  { source: 'products', type: 'sheet', table: 'products_sheet', tab: 'products' },
  { source: 'customers', type: 'csv', table: 'customers_csv', file: 'customers.csv' },
  { source: 'orders', type: 'csv', table: 'orders_csv', file: 'orders.csv' },
  { source: 'order_items', type: 'csv', table: 'order_items_csv', file: 'order_items.csv' },
  { source: 'payments', type: 'api', table: 'payments_api', api_source: 'payments',
    columns: ['order_id', 'payment_sequential', 'payment_type', 'payment_installments', 'payment_value'] },
  { source: 'reviews', type: 'api', table: 'reviews_api', api_source: 'reviews',
    columns: ['review_id', 'order_id', 'review_score', 'review_comment_title', 'review_comment_message',
              'review_creation_date', 'review_answer_timestamp'] },
  { source: 'geolocation', type: 'csv', table: 'geolocation_csv', file: 'geolocation.csv', batch_size: 5000 },
];

return sources
  .filter(s => ONLY.length === 0 || ONLY.includes(s.source))
  .map(s => ({ json: {
    ...s,
    run_id: runId,
    batch_size: s.batch_size ?? 2000,
    file_id: DRIVE_FILE_IDS[s.source] ?? null,
    spreadsheet_id: SPREADSHEET_ID,
    api_url: MOCK_API_URL,
    label: s.file ?? (s.tab ? `Sheet tab ${s.tab}` : `${s.api_source} API`),
  } }));

nodes.name: Sources
nodes.notes: Settings for the run. Fill in once: the 5 Drive file IDs, the spreadsheet ID and the mock API URL. Lists all 9 sources in load order (smallest first, geolocation last) with their type, raw table and batch size, and creates the run ID. To test a few sources only, put them in ONLY, e.g. ['sellers'].

nodes.name: Each source
nodes.notes: Loop Over Items, one source at a time, so only one source's data is in memory at once. 'loop' output = next source; 'done' output = all sources attempted.

nodes.name: By source type
nodes.notes: Switch: sends each source to the loader for its type: csv, sheet or api.

nodes.name: Load CSV from Drive
nodes.notes: Calls the sub-workflow 'Collection · Load CSV from Drive' for this source and waits for it to finish. Set to continue on error, so one failing source does not stop the others.

nodes.name: Load Sheet tab
nodes.notes: Calls the sub-workflow 'Collection · Load Sheet tab' for this source and waits for it to finish. Set to continue on error.

nodes.name: Load API source
nodes.notes: Calls the sub-workflow 'Collection · Load API source' for this source and waits for it to finish. Set to continue on error.

nodes.name: Check result
nodes.notes: Combines the source's settings with what the loader returned and marks it failed: true if the loader returned an error or nothing.

nodes.name: Failed?
nodes.notes: true → log the failure, then continue with the next source. false → continue with the next source.

nodes.name: Failure log row
nodes.notes: Builds an ops.agent_logs row with status 'failed' and the error message.

nodes.name: Log failure
nodes.notes: Writes the failure row into ops.agent_logs, then goes back to 'Each source'.

nodes.name: Loaded sources
nodes.notes: Keeps only the sources that loaded successfully. Failed sources get no data contract.

nodes.name: Each loaded source
nodes.notes: Loop Over Items over the loaded sources, one at a time, to write a data contract for each. 'done' output continues to the cross-source checks.

parameters.query:
=-- Profile every column of the raw table, whatever its columns are
select key as column_name,
       count(*) as total_rows,
       count(*) filter (where value is null or btrim(value) = '') as blank_values,
       count(distinct value) as distinct_values,
       (array_agg(distinct left(value, 60)) filter (where value is not null and btrim(value) <> ''))[1:8] as example_values
from raw.{{ $json.table }} t,
     jsonb_each_text(to_jsonb(t) - '_run_id' - '_loaded_at' - 'raw_record')
group by key
order by key;

nodes.name: Profile columns
nodes.notes: SQL profile of the raw table: per column, the number of rows, blank values and distinct values, plus up to 8 example values. Works for any raw table without knowing its columns.

nodes.name: Sample rows
nodes.notes: Takes 20 random rows from the raw table (random, because the first rows are rarely typical). Runs once per source.

nodes.name: Build contract prompt
nodes.notes: Puts the profile and the sample into one prompt for the Contract agent. Long text is cut to 200 characters. The whole table is never sent to the LLM.

options.systemMessage:
You are the collection agent in a data pipeline. You write a data contract for one raw data source.
The raw table stores every value as text exactly as it arrived; nothing has been cleaned.
Use only the column profile and the sample rows you are given. Do not invent columns or numbers.
For each column, state what it should contain once clean (expected_type: text, integer, decimal, timestamp, date, boolean, json) and whether it may be empty.
List the problems you can actually see (mixed date formats, numbers stored with units or commas, inconsistent spellings, negative values, blanks, repeated header rows, renamed keys in raw_record, likely duplicates).
Keep descriptions short and plain.

nodes.name: Contract agent
nodes.notes: AI agent (FR-C2) that writes the source's data contract: grain, likely key, the expected type of each column once clean, and the problems it can see. Returns structured JSON in the format of 'Contract output format'.

nodes.name: Contract model
nodes.notes: The LLM the Contract agent uses (Claude Sonnet 5.5, temperature 0 for consistent answers). Needs the Anthropic credential. Replace this node to use OpenAI instead.

nodes.name: Contract output format
nodes.notes: Structured Output Parser: forces the Contract agent's answer into fixed JSON (source, grain, likely_primary_key, row_count, columns, quality_flags, summary), so it can be stored and read reliably.

nodes.name: Contract row
nodes.notes: Builds the ops.data_contracts row: run ID, source, raw table and the contract JSON.

nodes.name: Save data contract
nodes.notes: Writes the contract into ops.data_contracts, then goes back to 'Each loaded source'.

parameters.query:
=-- Cross-source checks on the raw data (FR-C3). Values are compared after trimming only.
with
orders      as (select distinct btrim(order_id) id, btrim(customer_id) customer_id from raw.orders_csv where btrim(coalesce(order_id, '')) not in ('', 'order_id')),
items       as (select distinct btrim(order_id) order_id, btrim(product_id) product_id, btrim(seller_id) seller_id from raw.order_items_csv where btrim(coalesce(order_id, '')) not in ('', 'order_id')),
customers   as (select distinct btrim(customer_id) id, lpad(btrim(customer_zip_code_prefix), 5, '0') zip from raw.customers_csv where btrim(coalesce(customer_id, '')) <> ''),
sellers     as (select distinct btrim(seller_id) id from raw.sellers_csv where btrim(coalesce(seller_id, '')) <> ''),
products    as (select distinct btrim(product_id) id, lower(btrim(product_category_name)) category from raw.products_sheet where btrim(coalesce(product_id, '')) <> ''),
categories  as (select distinct lower(btrim(product_category_name)) category from raw.category_translation_sheet),
geo         as (select distinct lpad(btrim(geolocation_zip_code_prefix), 5, '0') zip from raw.geolocation_csv)
select 'order_items → orders' as between_sources, 'order_id in order_items with no matching order' as check_name,
       count(*) as mismatches from (select distinct order_id from items) x where not exists (select 1 from orders o where o.id = x.order_id)
union all
select 'order_items → products', 'product_id in order_items with no matching product',
       count(*) from (select distinct product_id from items where product_id <> '') x where not exists (select 1 from products p where p.id = x.product_id)
union all
select 'order_items → sellers', 'seller_id in order_items with no matching seller',
       count(*) from (select distinct seller_id from items) x where not exists (select 1 from sellers s where s.id = x.seller_id)
union all
select 'orders → customers', 'customer_id in orders with no matching customer',
       count(*) from (select distinct customer_id from orders) x where not exists (select 1 from customers c where c.id = x.customer_id)
union all
select 'payments API → orders', 'order_id in payments with no matching order',
       count(*) from (select distinct btrim(order_id) id from raw.payments_api where order_id is not null) x where not exists (select 1 from orders o where o.id = x.id)
union all
select 'reviews API → orders', 'order_id in reviews with no matching order',
       count(*) from (select distinct btrim(order_id) id from raw.reviews_api where order_id is not null) x where not exists (select 1 from orders o where o.id = x.id)
union all
select 'orders → payments API', 'orders with no payment record',
       count(*) from orders o where not exists (select 1 from raw.payments_api p where btrim(p.order_id) = o.id)
union all
select 'products sheet → category tab', 'product categories with no English translation',
       count(*) from (select distinct category from products where category <> '') x where not exists (select 1 from categories c where c.category = x.category)
union all
select 'category tab', 'categories translated more than once',
       count(*) from (select lower(btrim(product_category_name)) from raw.category_translation_sheet group by 1 having count(*) > 1) x
union all
select 'customers → geolocation', 'customer zip prefixes not found in geolocation',
       count(*) from (select distinct zip from customers) x where not exists (select 1 from geo g where g.zip = x.zip)
union all
select 'payments API schema', 'records where payment_value arrived under a different key',
       count(*) from raw.payments_api where payment_value is null and raw_record ? 'paymentValue'
union all
select 'reviews API schema', 'records where review_score arrived under a different key',
       count(*) from raw.reviews_api where review_score is null and raw_record ? 'reviewScore'
union all
select 'payments API schema', 'empty records',
       count(*) from raw.payments_api where raw_record = '{}'::jsonb
union all
select 'reviews API schema', 'empty records',
       count(*) from raw.reviews_api where raw_record = '{}'::jsonb;

nodes.name: Cross-source checks
nodes.notes: SQL that compares the raw tables with each other (FR-C3). It looks for: IDs with no match in the related table, orders with no payment, categories with no translation, zip codes missing from geolocation, renamed or missing keys and empty records in the APIs. Values are only trimmed, not cleaned.

nodes.name: Build mismatch prompt
nodes.notes: Puts the check results and the list of loaded sources into one prompt for the Mismatch agent.

options.systemMessage:
You are the collection agent in a data pipeline. You review checks that compare raw data sources with each other.
The values have only been trimmed; formatting differences (case, leading zeros, extra spaces) are still present and can cause mismatches.
Flag every check with mismatches > 0. Say which sources disagree, how many records, the most likely cause, and what the cleaning stage should do.
Use only the numbers you are given. Do not fix anything yourself.

nodes.name: Mismatch agent
nodes.notes: AI agent (FR-C3) that reviews the cross-source checks and flags every mismatch. For each one it gives the sources involved, how many records, likely cause and suggested action for the cleaning stage. It does not fix anything.

nodes.name: Mismatch model
nodes.notes: The LLM the Mismatch agent uses (Claude Sonnet 5.5, temperature 0). Needs the Anthropic credential.

nodes.name: Mismatch output format
nodes.notes: Structured Output Parser: forces the Mismatch agent's answer into fixed JSON (a list of mismatches plus a summary).

nodes.name: Mismatch row
nodes.notes: Builds the ops.data_contracts row for the mismatch report, with source '_cross_source'.

nodes.name: Save mismatch report
nodes.notes: Writes the mismatch report into ops.data_contracts.

nodes.name: Run log row
nodes.notes: Builds the final ops.agent_logs row for the whole run: how many sources loaded, total rows, how many mismatches were flagged, and which sources failed.

nodes.name: Log run
nodes.notes: Writes the run's final row into ops.agent_logs (action 'run_complete'). This is the last step of the collection stage.
